stories.headline: Scott Colom takes a Senate seat in Mississippi
stories.summary: Scott Colom, a Democratic district attorney, has won a United States Senate seat in Mississippi. He defeated the Republican incumbent Cindy Hyde-Smith in what was considered an upset, after more than a week of ballot counting. He is the first African American senator elected in the state since 1874.

stories.headline: Sudan lifts its ban on tea from Kenya
stories.summary: Sudan has agreed to lift its ban on imports of tea from Kenya, which had stood for 20 months. The deal was signed by the Kenyan president, William Ruto.

stories.headline: A car boot sixpence carries a minting mystery
stories.summary: A silver sixpence issued during the reign of King William IV was found in an album of coins at a car boot sale in Greater Manchester. Researchers have now measured the damage to its portrait side, where the difference between the highest and lowest points reaches about 0.75 millimetres.

sources.excerpt: The 2026 United States Senate election in Mississippi was held on November 3, 2026, to elect a member of the United States Senate to represent the state of Mississippi. Democratic district attorney Scott Colom defeated Republican incumbent Cindy Hyde-Smith in what was considered an upset.
After more than a week of ballot counting, Colom was projected the winner on November 11.

Colom is the first Democrat elected to the Senate in Mississippi since 1982, the first African American senator elected in the state since 1874, and the first African American senator ever elected in the state by popular vote.
Kenyan president William Ruto signs a deal for Sudan to lift its 20-month ban on imports of tea from Kenya.

The coin was found in an album containing various coins at a car boot sale in Greater Manchester, England. Although the sixpence had an individual price tag of £8, the entire album was subsequently purchased as a single lot rather than the coin being bought separately.
